Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 24-Dec-2024 (02:30 PM - 05:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  FIFTH SEMESTER B.Tech. (IT) EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2024 / JANUARY 2025  
  SUBJECT: ICT 3122/IT_3122 - PRINCIPLES OF OPERATING SYSTEMS  
  (MAKEUP)  
  
  
  PRINCIPLES OF OPERATING SYSTEMS [ICT 3122]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                       Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               Consider the following scenario: A user clicks to open a file in a text editor. The text editor loads the (5)  
  file, but it needs to wait for the disk to read the data. Identify the state of the process at each stage  
  and explain the transitions involved with neat diagram.  
1B)               With the help of an example, explain the roles of the UNIX kernel and UNIX shell in the functioning       (3)  
  of the operating system.  
1C)               Explain how seek time and rotational latency affect disk performance. Propose the strategies that         (2)  
  the operating system might employ to minimize seek time and improve overall disk access  
  efficiency.  
2A)               A system has five fixed-size memory partitions of sizes 100 KB, 500 KB, 200 KB, 300 KB, and 600           (5)  
  KB (in order). The following processes arrive and request memory:  
  
  Process A: 212 KB (Arrival Time: 0)  
  Process B: 417 KB (Arrival Time: 2)  
  Process C: 112 KB (Arrival Time: 4)  
  Process D: 426 KB (Arrival Time: 6)  
  Process E: 330 KB (Arrival Time: 10)  
  
  At time 5, Process A finishes and releases its memory partition.  
  Using First-fit, Best-fit, and Worst-fit memory allocation strategies, perform the following:  
  i) With a neat diagram show which partition each process will be allocated to for each of the three  
  strategies.  
  ii) Calculate the remaining sizes of memory partitions after all allocations are made for each  
  strategy.  
  iii) Calculate the internal fragmentation on memory utilization for each strategy.  
  iv) Compare which strategy leaves the most and least memory unused after process E is allocated,  
  considering internal fragmentation.  
  
  
2B)               A system has 120 available memory frames and is running four processes, P1, P2, P3, and P4, with (3)  
  the following memory requirements Process P1: 100 KB, Process P2: 200 KB, Process P3: 300 KB,  
  Process P4: 150 KB  
  
  i) Determine the number of frames allocated to each process using the equal allocation strategy.  
  ii) Determine the number of frames allocated to each process using the proportional allocation  
  strategy.  
  iii) Propose an alternative method for the proportional allocation scheme. Justify how this alternative  
  method could improve system performance.  
  
  Page 1 of 3

2C)   Consider the following situation where a process P1, uses the swap-based algorithm to acquire a             (2)  
  lock:  
  
  
  P1 is preempted right after modifying shared_data but before releasing the lock.  
  A second process, P2, is scheduled and tries to acquire the lock  
  Answer the following:  
  i) Determine if P2 acquires the lock while P1 is preempted? Justify  
  ii) Identify if P2 be able to proceed into the critical section? Justify.  
3A)   Identify scenarios where deferred cancellation of threads be preferable over asynchronous                   (5)  
  cancellation, and why? Justify with a real-world example where deferred cancellation improves  
  resource management.  
3B)   Check whether the system is in a safe state by applying the deadlock avoidance algorithm. If so,            (3)  
  obtain the safe sequence for the below data. Number of instances of each resource type X=10,  
  Y=7, Z=11. Show the detailed steps.  
  
  
3C)   Compare and contrast between hard, firm and soft real time systems, highlighting their key                  (2)  
  characteristics and use cases.  
4A)   Given a system with 3 frames, apply the FIFO, Optimal and LRU Page Replacement Algorithm to                 (5)  
  the reference string 5, 3, 2, 1, 4, 2, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 5, 3. Illustrate how pages are replaced and calculate  
  the total number of page faults including initial page faults when the frame is free.  
4B)   Analyze how the dual-mode operation in operating systems improves system security. Provide a                (3)  
  real-world example to demonstrate how these modes are enforced.  
4C)   Compare the pros and cons of using a tree-structured directory versus a single-level directory              (2)  
  structure.  
5A)   Propose a solution to the Dining Philosophers problem using monitors. Explain how the monitor's             (5)  
  condition variables ensure that philosophers alternate between thinking and eating without causing  
  deadlock or starvation.  
5B)   Given a system with 5 processes (P0, P1, P2, P3, P4) and 3 resource types (A, B, C) with the                (3)  
  following allocation and maximum matrix:  
  $$Available resources: A=2,B=2,C=1$$  
  
  
  Page 2 of 3

i) Calculate the Need matrix for the given system.  
  ii) Determine whether the system is in a safe state using the Banker's Algorithm.  
5C)   Apply the Earliest Deadline First (EDF) scheduling algorithm to the following set of tasks:   (2)  
  
  Task 1: Execution time = 2 ms, Deadline = 10 ms  
  Task 2: Execution time = 1 ms, Deadline = 5 ms  
  Task 3: Execution time = 3 ms, Deadline = 15 ms.  
  
  Create a schedule for these tasks and determine whether all tasks meet their deadlines.  
  
  
  -----End-----
